_provenance: Q14 defect-region corners (#192). `over-depth` and the Loc.base=-1 widening are NOT here: both require crossing MAX_DEPTH (256), so their inputs are ~2-6 KB and are generated in test/unit/explain-defects.test.ts rather than pinned as literals. Inputs are the phase-0 mutation suite's parents with one controlled defect injected, plus the coordinate-pass classes. `defects` is the merged, source-ordered output of segmentStatements + resolveStatements + resolveDocument + resolveSymbols over the input. Offsets are analyzed bytes, half-open, as contracted in src/explain/coordinates.ts.

corners.name: unbalanced-close-marks-the-stray-delimiter
corners.why: the injected `)` is the defect; the region is exactly that byte

corners.name: unterminated-string-spans-the-swallowed-run
corners.why: the region runs from the opening quote to end of input — the text the scan swallowed — not just the quote byte

corners.name: unclosed-bracket-marks-its-opener
corners.why: an unclosed delimiter's defect is AT THE OPENER: where it was supposed to close is exactly what is unknown, so the opener is the only honest location

corners.name: unclosed-brace-marks-its-opener
corners.why: same rule as the bracket; the note channel fuses these into one `unclosed:{` string with no offset at all

corners.name: bad-escape-marks-the-backslash
corners.why: symbols.ts is the only scanner that detects this class; the device errors at the escape and classes every later byte `none`

corners.name: bom-is-its-own-class-not-non-ascii
corners.why: U+FEFF is 3 UTF-8 bytes; in LEADING position it is a `bom` and is NOT also reported as `non-ascii`

corners.name: non-ascii-value-is-a-positional-fact
corners.why: examples.md example 22 — a legal command. The 4 UTF-8 bytes of the astral char are 4 analyzed bytes. isPositionalFact() must keep this out of error severity.

corners.name: non-ascii-runs-coalesce
corners.why: three adjacent 2-byte characters are ONE region, not three — a CJK comment must not produce one defect per code point

corners.name: a-defect-inside-a-non-ascii-statement-keeps-its-precise-offset
corners.input: :foreach i in="ä" do={ /ip route add x=1) }
corners.why: the segmenter's own defects always come from the TOP-LEVEL scan, which works in analyzed bytes throughout, so a non-ASCII statement never widens them. Only the walker-raised classes (over-depth) can reach the Loc.base=-1 fallback.

corners.name: a-bare-apostrophe-is-not-a-token
corners.why: #355 — `'` is not a RouterOS string delimiter and not a legal bare byte. The region is the apostrophe itself, which is the byte the device's own column names.
corners.verified: CHR 7.21.5/7.23.5/7.24.2/7.25beta3: `expected end of command (line 1 column 30)`, byte-identical on all four. Column 30 is 1-based, so offset 29 — the apostrophe.

corners.name: only-the-first-apostrophe-is-reported
corners.why: #355 — classification stops at the first one, as with the hard `#`, so a second occurrence is not an independent finding.
corners.verified: CHR 7.21.5/7.23.5/7.24.2/7.25beta3: `expected end of command (line 1 column 30)` — the device reports the FIRST apostrophe here too, not the trailing one.

corners.name: balanced-apostrophes-are-rejected-too
corners.why: #355 — the control that makes this a LEXICAL rule rather than a quote-balance one. A balance rule would accept this pair; the device does not.
corners.verified: CHR 7.21.5/7.23.5/7.24.2/7.25beta3: `syntax error (line 1 column 27)`, byte-identical on all four.

corners.name: balanced-apostrophes-in-a-directive-are-rejected-too
corners.why: #355 — the same balanced pair in a `:` directive, so the rule is not about argument pairing either.
corners.verified: CHR 7.21.5/7.23.5/7.24.2/7.25beta3: `syntax error (line 1 column 6)`, byte-identical on all four.

corners.name: an-apostrophe-inside-a-string-is-legal
corners.why: #355 ACCEPTING control — only `"` opens a string, and inside one the apostrophe is ordinary content. The string run is consumed whole before the lexical branch sees it.
corners.verified: CHR 7.21.5/7.23.5/7.24.2/7.25beta3: parses to `(evl /ip/address/addaddress=1.1.1.1;32;comment=it's here)` on all four.

corners.name: an-apostrophe-inside-a-comment-is-legal
corners.why: #355 ACCEPTING control — the comment run is consumed whole too. This is the case that broke the retired quote-count preflight, which read the contraction as an unclosed quote.
corners.verified: CHR 7.21.5/7.23.5/7.24.2/7.25beta3: parses to `(evl /ip/address/print)` on all four.

corners.name: clean-input-has-no-defects
corners.why: the floor: valid input carries no region at all
